summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Avalon Cloud to explore a cloud+GPU provider partnership. Discussed go-to-market model (marketplace listing, referral/discount), technical integration patterns (VPC peering, private control plane, KMS integration), benchmark requirements, and a pilot scope for a joint customer. Agreed on follow-ups: share partner docs, infra checklist, and schedule a technical deep dive next week.
transcript:
Meeting start - 2026-05-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Shaw (Redwood SE), Priya Reddy (Avalon Head of Partnerships), Samir Patel (Avalon CTO), Diego Morales (Avalon SE)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, this is Marcus on the SE side. How are you all?
[00:07] Priya Reddy: Hi Lena, hi Marcus, doing well, thanks. Excited to chat — we've been following Redwood's infra posts.
[00:12] Marcus Shaw: Nice, thanks Priya. Quick agenda, 1) partner models, 2) tech integration, 3) pilot scope, 4) next steps. Does that work?
[00:20] Samir Patel: Yep sounds good. Diego's on to cover some infra details if needed.
[00:25] Diego Morales: hi all, loud and clear.
[00:30] Lena Park: Cool. Priya, maybe start with a bit about Avalon — your cloud + gpu focus and the sort of partners you typically look for?
[00:36] Priya Reddy: Sure, quick rundown — Avalon Cloud is region-focused provider in EMEA and APAC, we operate custom racks with H100 and A100 clusters, we also do managed kubernetes. We see a lot of ML infra demand from fintech and health customers. We're looking for inference partners to add to our marketplace and reference architecture.
[00:55] Marcus Shaw: Nice, that matches a lot of folks we work with. For context, Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated capacity, and a private deployment model so we can support a marketplace integration or a co-managed private control plane.
[01:12] Samir Patel: When you say private control plane, do you mean we get to host the control plane in our VPC? We're sensitive about customer data residency and need to know what parts talk back to Redwood.
[01:24] Marcus Shaw: Good question. We offer a private deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed (installed in your VPC) or a hybrid with private networking to Redwood's control plane. There are tradeoffs — with fully customer-managed you keep full network isolation but we lose some automatic telemetry unless you opt-in to sending metrics.
[01:42] Priya Reddy: For marketplace customers we prefer some managed telemetry but with strict KMS separation. Do you have KMS/HSM integrations?
[01:49] Lena Park: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and support bring-your-own HSM for private deployments; our audit logs and key access controls can be configured per-customer. We'll share the security checklist.
[01:59] Diego Morales: ok thanks, curious on how you handle model variants for capacity constrained nodes — like do you fallback to quantized variants or smaller models automatically?
[02:08] Marcus Shaw: We have smart routing and automatic fallbacks. For example requests can route by cost or latency; there's a policy engine that can fallback to a compatible quantized variant or different family. Also we do KV cache prefixing to lower token costs for repeated prompts.
[02:22] Samir Patel: nv — you mentioned KV cache — we log it as 'K-V cash' in our infra docs sometimes whoops, but ok.
[02:29] (laughter)
[02:31] Priya Reddy: On the business side, what's the go-to-market model? Are you looking for revenue split on marketplace usage or more of a referral model?
[02:40] Lena Park: We do flexible models — marketplace listing with per-call routing and revenue share, or referrals with discounted committed capacity for Avalon customers on Dedicated. There's also co-selling and joint account exec motion for enterprise deals. We'll send a partner one-pager with options.
[02:56] Priya Reddy: Great. For pricing, curious about unit economics — we need rough token cost vs dedicated capacity baseline to build an offering on top.
[03:05] Marcus Shaw: We'll share sample cost sheets; dedicated committed pools change the per-token math quite a bit, and quantized 4-bit models reduce inference cost significantly. But it depends on sequence lengths and batching.
[03:18] Samir Patel: Speaking of batching, how does your autoscaling and burst capacity work? Our customers expect predictable latency for peak trading windows.
[03:27] Marcus Shaw: We support configurable autoscaling and burst capacity for Dedicated. There's also a burst policy you can set for SLAs; in practice we size reserved pools to match baseline, and allow bursts to shared capacity if you'd like lower committed cost.
[03:41] Diego Morales: what's the typical latency SLO on H100 for a gpt-like model at 2k tokens?
[03:48] Marcus Shaw: Roughly in the 150-300ms per-token range for streaming setups; end-to-end depends on networking. We'll provide benchmark artifacts.
[03:56] Priya Reddy: On the security side, SOC2 type 2 and ISO? We need to show compliance to some of our enterprise buyers.
[04:04] Lena Park: Redwood has SOC2 and is pursuing ISO certs; for Private deployments you get audit log options and segregated encryption keys. We'll attach the certs and compliance pack.
[04:15] Priya Reddy: Nice. For integration, we're thinking two possible flows: 1) marketplace listing where Avalon forwards inference calls to Redwood hosted endpoints (with VPC peering and private IPs), 2) white-labeled private deployment customers can choose to spin up Redwood private control plane on Avalon. Thoughts?
[04:32] Marcus Shaw: Both are doable. The marketplace flow is faster to market — you can onboard customers to Redwood hosted instances routed from Avalon. VPC peering + private link reduces egress concerns. The private deployment is longer but gives full isolation — we'd work with your infra team on orchestration.
[04:48] Samir Patel: For the marketplace flow, how do billing and metering work? Does Avalon need to mediate billing or can Redwood invoice end-customers?
[04:56] Lena Park: Flexible. We can route usage into partner billing (we provide metering exports and invoice Avalon) or we can invoice end-customers directly and pay revenue share. Depends on compliance and your preferred model.
[05:08] Priya Reddy: Good. Let's talk about a pilot. We have one fintech customer that needs low-latency chat moderation and an embeddings pipeline for risk signals. They'd like a 6-week pilot to evaluate latency and cost.
[05:20] Marcus Shaw: Perfect — for pilot success we usually ask for: sample workload (qps, avg sequence length), SLOs for P95 latency, dataset for quality checks, and acceptance criteria.
[05:30] Diego Morales: we can provide qps peaks (200 qps), average sequence length ~512 tokens, occasional spikes to 1k. P95 target <600ms.
[05:40] Marcus Shaw: Great, that helps. For that workload we might recommend Dedicated reserved pool on A100 or H100 depending on latency requirements and model family. We'll run a benchmark on equivalent nodes.
[05:52] Samir Patel: Do you support on-prem or air-gapped installs? We do have a couple regulated customers asking for that.
[05:59] Marcus Shaw: Yes, Private can be deployed on-prem. The installer supports air-gapped node prep, but you do need to handle initial package transfer and key management. It's more effort but we have a repeatable process.
[06:12] Priya Reddy: Ok timeline — if pilot starts late May we want everything provisioned by early June. Is that realistic?
[06:20] Lena Park: Potentially yes; we have an onboarding runbook. Marcus will share infra checklist and estimated provisioning lead time.
[06:28] Marcus Shaw: I'll add node templates and terraform snippets. For H100 clusters, we usually recommend X nodes for 200 qps with 512 token median; will include suggested counts.
[06:39] (crosstalk)
[06:42] Samir Patel: Any limitations on model types — do you host closed-source models or only open family?
[06:47] Marcus Shaw: We support both; customers can bring their own models if licensing permits. We also maintain a catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For licensed models there are licensing steps.
[06:58] Priya Reddy: On observability, does Redwood emit per-route metrics so we can show latency in the Avalon console?
[07:05] Lena Park: Yes, we have per-route, per-model dashboards, traces, and token-level cost breakdowns. We can push metrics to a prometheus endpoint or stream to your observability pipeline.
[07:15] Diego Morales: that would be handy — our portal can surface usage if we can get prometheus or cloudwatch metrics.
[07:21] Marcus Shaw: We'll include example dashboards and recommended metrics to export.
[07:26] Priya Reddy: Competitors question: we've talked to Velascale and Aurora — how does Redwood differentiate?
[07:33] Lena Park: Mainly production-first focus: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, smart routing and cost controls, and an emphasis on observability and evals to prevent regressions. Also our GTM partner program is flexible for marketplace and referrals.
[07:48] Samir Patel: Nice. Any red flags we've missed — compliance or data residency concerns?
[07:55] Marcus Shaw: For data residency you can choose region pinned deployments; for full isolation use private control plane in your region. Also KMS separation ensures key ownership. We'll provide the compliance pack.
[08:07] Priya Reddy: Ok sounds good. Let's quick discuss commercial models again — if we do a marketplace listing what are the typical rev-shares you offer?
[08:17] Lena Park: Typically 10-30% depending on commitment and who manages billing; we'll propose a few tiers in the partner deck.
[08:25] Diego Morales: For pilot — what support level do we get? SE time, benchmarks, runbooks?
[08:30] Marcus Shaw: Pilot includes SE support for benching and onboarding, runbooks, and a short-term SLA. For expanded pilots we can scope dedicated engineering hours.
[08:40] Priya Reddy: ok great. I think that's enough to start. Can we recap next steps?
[08:45] Lena Park: Sure. Recap: 1) Lena to send partner one-pager + commercial tiers by 2026-05-17, 2) Marcus to share infra checklist, node templates, and benchmark artifacts by 2026-05-20, 3) Avalon to share pilot workload details and SLOs by 2026-05-19, 4) schedule technical deep-dive for week of 2026-05-25.
[09:08] Samir Patel: confirmed. Diego will coordinate infra availability.
[09:12] Priya Reddy: We'll also circulate a shortlist of initial customers for pilot.
[09:16] Lena Park: Awesome. Anything else?
[09:18] (brief pause)
[09:20] Marcus Shaw: One tiny note — if you'd like, we can run a small non-production benchmark on a sample H100 node within a week to validate latency assumptions.
[09:29] Samir Patel: that would be helpful, yes.
[09:31] Lena Park: Great. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. Thanks everyone.
[09:37] Priya Reddy: Thanks all, bye.
[09:39] Meeting end.

Notes/links referenced: Partner one-pager (link to be shared), infra checklist (terraform snippets), compliance pack (SOC2 artifact), sample benchmarks spreadsheet.

Transcript end.
